Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>

Subject: PrecisionMed — inference suitability brief + perf references

Hi Lena + team,

Thanks again for taking time today — quick recap from our call and the recommended next steps so your engineering team can evaluate Redwood for inference at PrecisionMed. I kept this short and attached the benchmark summary plus the prompt set we used for the throughput/latency runs.

What we covered (short):
- Primary workload: structured clinical note summarization + snippet extraction (avg input ~1.6k tokens, 99th ~4k)
- SLAs you mentioned: p99 latency target ~350ms and sustained TPS target ~45 rps for peak windows
- Data constraints: PHI, need VPC/private deployment for production (we covered Dedicated/Private options)

Recommended model slate for initial pilot (ranked by cost/latency/quality trade-off):
1) rw-instruct-7B-q4f (Redwood-verified) — best balance of quality and 95–99% latency headroom; good for early pilot
2) llama2-13b-redwood-q4_1 — higher single-request quality for longer contexts; expect ~1.6x latency relative to 7B on same hardware
3) rw-instruct-3B-quant — very low-cost/high-tps option for bulk extraction passes (useful for batch pre-processing)

What I attached/shared:
- precisionmed_benchmark_summary.pdf (quick TPS / p50 / p90 / p99 snapshots for the three models above, measured on A100-equivalent pool)
- precisionmed_prompt_set_v1.jsonl (the prompt/test set we used; includes edge-case notes)
- Redwood-verified perf profiles: full interactive link below

Quick highlights from the perf run (summary):
- rw-instruct-7B-q4f: sustained 52 TPS, p50=62ms, p90=128ms, p99=312ms (seq len median 1.4k)
- llama2-13b-redwood-q4_1: sustained 28 TPS, p50=120ms, p90=240ms, p99=560ms
- rw-instruct-3B-quant: sustained 120 TPS (batch-optimized), p99=180ms (for short contexts)

Notes on quality/regression guardrails:
- We run continuous regression checks against your baseline prompt set and can gate model rollouts on quality metrics (F1/ROUGE thresholds plus a manual review bucket).
- Redwood Optimize will surface prompt regressions and model-drift alerts; we can push alerts to your Slack + create HubSpot tickets for follow-up.

Next steps I suggest:
1) Share these artifacts with your ML infra + security team (I included Marissa/Ben on this thread for technical follow-up)
2) Confirm whether you want a full pilot on Dedicated or start with Hosted API for an instrumentation pass
3) We can set up a 60–90 minute technical workshop (throughput run + latency traces) next week — propose Tue 12/1 or Wed 12/2, 10–11:30 PT

Attachments: see zip of attached PDFs in the Drive folder linked below.

Best,
Ava

Lena — quick answers inline and links to the artifacts you asked for.

> 1) Regression detection: can you confirm how Redwood computes the "quality regression" signal (we need something auditable for clinical QA)?

Short answer: yes — the signal is configurable and auditable. Details: we run per-prompt metric baselining (you can choose metrics: F1, ROUGE-L, exact-match, BLEU) and track distribution shifts using population statistics + rolling-window hypothesis tests. We store evaluation snapshots with diffs and a human-review queue. Everything is exportable (CSV / JSON) with timestamps for audits. See the technical note in the Drive link (folder -> /audit-regression-notes.md).

> 2) Data retention & logs: our security team will need confirmation of how ephemeral KV/cache items are handled and retention (we are thinking <30 days for any request traces).

We support Private/Dedicated deployments with customer-managed VPC and KMS. By default request traces + KV cache metadata are retained 7 days; retention windows are configurable up to 90 days for audit purposes. For PHI workloads we recommend enabling on-prem/private with our minimal-retention profile (we'll add the exact policy text to the Drive folder).

> 3) Cost: back-of-envelope monthly estimate for rw-instruct-7B-q4f pilot at 45 sustained TPS + Dedicated minimum commit?

Estimate (very rough):
- Pilot (Hosted API, instrumentation + eval runs): ~ $10k–$15k/month including evaluation credit (depends on average response lengths)
- Dedicated (reserved capacity to hit sustained 45 TPS with p99 ~350ms): ballpark $85k–$120k/month depending on autoscaling headroom and GPU class.

I uploaded a short cost worksheet to the Drive link and the Redwood perf profile page includes per-token throughput curves so your infra folks can model costs precisely. Links below:
- Perf profiles + raw traces: https://redwood-internal.s3.amazonaws.com/benchmarks/precisionmed/20261127/perf_profiles.html
- Drive folder (artifacts + regression note): https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3c-precisionmed-eval
- HubSpot deal: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/0-1234567/deal/5372

Proposed times for the technical workshop: Wed 12/2 09:00–10:30 PT or Wed 12/2 13:00–14:30 PT. Marissa / Ben — can you confirm availability and whether you prefer Dedicated pilot or Hosted instrumentation?

Thanks — happy to jump on a quick sync if any of these points need expansion.

Best,
Ava
